comment_box: Removing access to care for women, especially women veterans, is REPREHENSIBLE.  For the Veterans themselves   The stated reasoning is so that the "VA provides only needed medical services to our nation's heroes and their families."  Access to care for women in all of its forms is a NEEDED medical service. "Abortion bans and restrictions harm maternal health in two key ways: staying pregnant when wanting an abortion exposes people to pregnancy-related risks they otherwise would not have had and, within such a worsening environment for healthcare, pregnancies themselves are riskier." Additionally, Biggs et al. found that women who wanted to get an abortion, but were denied one, initially experienced more anxiety symptoms and stress, lower self-esteem, and less life satisfaction than those who received one.2 Over time, those same women developed more physical health problems than those who received abortions, and two of them later died from complications related to childbirth.3"  We are not second-class citizens.  For the members who separate from the service but are authorized VA care or members whose families are authorized VA care, you are removing an important and valuable care component.  This IS providing a NEEDED medical service to those who choose it.
